title: Stage 4 decision bundle journal
description: The one decision bundle the operator most recently authorised, and how far its operations got (#173). ⚠️ WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST PROJECT MUTATION AND AFTER EVERY OPERATION, so a crash or a compaction between two operations leaves a record of exactly which ones ran. ⚠️ IT HOLDS THE APPROVED WORDING AND NOTHING KILN OBSERVED: operation arguments are what the operator confirmed, and a failure is recorded as a stable code, never as an error message, a path or a tool result. ⚠️ HOST-LOCAL AND NEVER COMMITTED. An authorisation is one operator's answer on one computer; a clone that inherited it would resume a bundle nobody there approved.

digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical stage, reserved ids and ordered operations. A request whose digest differs is a different bundle and needs its own approval.

status.description: `authorized` and `failed` are resumable under the same digest. `blocked` means the project no longer matches what was approved, so the authorisation is spent.

targets.description: Every artifact or stage document this bundle touches, with the content hash it must have right now: `null` while an artifact is still to be created. A resume compares these before continuing.

args.description: The operation's approved arguments, exactly as the confirmation showed them. Open because each typed writer validates its own.

code.description: A stable refusal code. ⚠️ A CODE AND NEVER A MESSAGE: an error message can carry a path or a credential.
